nodes.label: Agent decides when and what; Step Functions decides how
nodes.norm_label: agent decides when and what; step functions decides how
nodes.rationale: Probabilistic token generators make poor distributed transaction coordinators; prompt rules are aspirations, while IAM scoping, ARN pinning and ASL validation are enforced contracts.

nodes.label: stateMachineArn pinning in Gateway target
nodes.rationale: The Gateway strips the pinned parameter from the tool schema and injects the ARN at invocation, so the agent cannot choose or override which state machine it triggers.

nodes.label: Express Workflow
nodes.rationale: Express pushes logs asynchronously to CloudWatch Logs and does not support DescribeExecution or GetExecutionHistory in the same way, so it is avoided for agent-monitored pipelines.

nodes.label: Standard Workflow
nodes.rationale: Glue and Redshift jobs can exceed the 5-minute Express limit; Standard keeps full history queryable through DescribeExecution and GetExecutionHistory.

nodes.label: Two-tier least-privilege IAM design
nodes.rationale: State-machine and execution ARN formats are evaluated separately; scoping execution ARNs to the state machine name blocks StopExecution against other workflows.

nodes.label: Working Rules
nodes.rationale: Keep IAM least-privilege, do not hardcode AWS account IDs or ARNs (use .env and SAM parameters), do not commit .env or credentials, and keep WorkflowFailed as an explicit Fail state.

nodes.label: Operational Risk and Mitigation Matrix
nodes.rationale: IAM policies and deterministic workflow boundaries matter more than system prompt instructions; prompt injection can bypass prompt rules.
